course_description:
Development of classical instrumental, vocal, or compositional technique through individual instruction, ensemble participation and practical application. For instrumentalists and vocalists, this includes the refinement of technical skills, historical performance practices, and interpretation of canonical works across various stylistic periods.

Vocal studies further incorporate language and diction training appropriate to the classical repertoire.

For composers, skills in notation, compositional approaches, responding to stimulus and orchestration are developed, along with understanding of a range of contemporary styles and genres, focusing on developing skills appropriate for your own practice.

This course develops classical instrumental, vocal, or compositional skills through individual instruction, ensemble participation, and practical performance activities. Instrumental and vocal studies focus on the development of technical proficiency, stylistic awareness, historical performance practices, and the interpretation of repertoire from a range of musical periods.

Vocal studies additionally develop language, diction, and communication skills relevant to the performance of classical repertoire.

Composition studies focus on the development of notation, orchestration, compositional techniques, and creative responses to a range of stimuli. Students explore diverse contemporary styles and genres while developing approaches that support their individual creative practice.

course_aims: This foundational course develops your capacity and ability to perform with confidence from technical and musical perspectives and to rehearse and perform as part of an ensemble.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate a foundational level of artistry and technical fluency as a solo performer
Identify your progress at a foundational level towards being a professional musician.
Demonstrate a foundational level of artistry as an ensemble performer and your awareness of professional expectations surrounding ensemble performance in varied contexts at a foundational level

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Performance Workshop Students in all Performance Studies courses are expected to attend the weekly workshop for their instrument group: Brass Composition Piano Lower Strings Upper Strings Percussion Reeds Voice Flutes Learning outcomes: L01, L02

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Practical Lessons Students receive 12 one-hour lessons with an allocated teacher throughout the semester. Lessons are usually scheduled weekly during semester. Allocated teachers may agree to a different schedule if requested. The allocated teacher will advise if it is possible to reschedule lessons. Lessons are usually rescheduled only because of unforeseen circumstances, such as sudden illness. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Cohort Collaboration Ensemble All performance students are required to attend a weekly 2hr ensemble class in the period outlined relevant to their discipline. The information below offers a broad guide to activities and further information will be made available on Blackboard: Brass Flutes Percussion Reeds Saxophone Strings Composition The contemporary ensemble class focuses on new compositions, contributed by members as well as drawn from international twenty-first century repertoire. Composition students in all Performance Studies courses are expected to attend the weekly classes, and to both play in and compose for the ensemble. The ensemble is open to any instrument or voice type, and students who are not studying composition are encouraged to participate and to compose new works for the ensemble. Within the Sketch Ensemble, there will be a separate Sketch Production Ensemble for approved students. Lyric Diction for Voice Students Voice students in Performance Studies courses 1-3 are expected to attend the weekly class on language and diction. The aim of the workshops is to develop proficiency and competence in the major operatic languages (Italian in course 1, German in course 2, French in course 3) so that students can perform in these languages with a high degree of accuracy and confidence. Students are taught the phonetic representation and correct physiological formation of sounds of each of these languages, and practice songs in these languages. Piano Collaborative Class Piano students in all Performance Studies courses are expected to attend the weekly piano collaborative class. Piano students are assigned duo or trio work with an instrumentalist or vocalist, and work with their nominated collaborative artist(s). Piano students may be expected to attend one-on-one lessons for their collaborative partner(s) and to have their collaborative partner(s) attend their one-on-one lessons. Students are welcome to attend as many classes relevant to their skills as they wish. However they will only be assessed on one activity. All students are strongly encouraged to attend and participate in the Contemporary Music Ensemble and Piano Collaborative Class even if they are being assessed in other groups. All students must attend and participate in any performances linked to these learning activities including Project Week. Learning outcomes: L02, L03

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Nickson Room Concerts Students in all Performance Studies courses are encouraged to attend the public concerts in the Nickson Room every Thursday during semester. Please see Blackboard for further details. Learning outcomes: L02, L03

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Exam week 2
learning_activities.topic: Private Practice Students are expected to practice intensively throughout the semester, including non-teaching weeks. Please ask your teachers for advice about the appropriate frequency and length of practice time for your instrument, voice or composition studies. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Project Week Each semester, the School of Music suspends its regular teaching program for one week to present a program of special events, ensemble rehearsals, seminars, workshops, and performances. Activities take place across a range of on-campus and external venues, with the schedule and locations published on Blackboard. Students are expected to attend and participate in all seminars, presentations, rehearsals, and performances relevant to their principal area of study. These activities form an integral part of the learning experience and provide opportunities for collaborative performance, professional development, and engagement with the broader School of Music community. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
